what_its_for: Eslicarbazepine is a seizure medicine (anticonvulsant) used to treat partial-onset seizures in adults and children 4 years of age and older. It helps calm down abnormal electrical activity in the brain that causes seizures.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth once a day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole, or you may crush it and mix it with water or soft food like applesauce if you have trouble swallowing. Always take it at the same time each day to keep the medicine working evenly in your body.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over a few weeks to find the right amount for you. Adults usually start at 400 mg once daily and may go up to 800 mg to 1600 mg once daily. Children's doses are based on their body weight. Never change your dose on your own — always follow your doctor's instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do NOT take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original container, tightly closed, away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can increase dizziness and drowsiness. Be careful driving, operating machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid stopping this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause more seizures.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: thoughts of suicide or hurting yourself, new or worsening depression or mood changes, severe skin rash, blistering, or peeling of the skin, fever with rash or swollen lymph nodes, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), unusual bruising or bleeding, very low sodium symptoms such as headache, nausea, confusion, or seizures that get worse, or signs of a serious allergic reaction like swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat.
when_it_works: This medicine starts working fairly quickly after you begin taking it, but it may take several weeks of dose adjustments before your seizures are fully under control. Do not stop taking it even if you feel well, as seizures can return if you miss doses or stop suddenly.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It may harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment. Breastfeeding: This medicine may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits. Older adults (65+): You may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness and low sodium levels. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose. Kidney problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if your kidneys do not work well. Children under 4: This medicine is not approved for children younger than 4 years old.
